title: Mark Player — notes pinned to the frame, then a ready rough cut (whiteboard)

carousel.rule: one PNG per scene = the last fully drawn frame of that scene, caption included

sections.music: ambient intro, no drums — slow drawing
full — the killer feature starts here
breakdown — lighter; fade out over the last 1.0 s

scenes.draw: A pile of video files (film-strip rectangles) grows. Two speech bubbles from a client: "fix it around minute two…" and "…where the drummer kicks in." A clock spins. No numbers anywhere.
scenes.caption: Client notes. No timecodes.
scenes.vo: Client notes without timecodes. Hours of footage to search.

scenes.draw: A simple player is drawn: frame, scrub bar, play triangle. Keycap M on the beat: a speech-note pin drops onto the bar with a timecode tag "00:01:59:10" and handwritten text "tighten here — on the snare". Then keycap F: a filled ★ flies onto the bar; keycap N: a ✗ flies onto the bar.

captions.text: Press M. Say what you mean.

scenes.vo: In Mark Player, press M and say what you mean — the note is pinned to the frame. F for the best, N for the misses.

scenes.draw: An arrow labeled ".xml" leads from the player to a long timeline track labeled "Premiere Pro". The pin, ★ and ✗ drop onto the track at exactly the same positions, each with a short tick to its frame.
scenes.caption: Export XML. Every note on its exact frame.
scenes.vo: Export XML — every note lands in Premiere on its exact frame.

scenes.draw: The same notes become a sheet of paper titled "review.txt" with lines like "00:01:59:10 — · Comment: tighten here — on the snare", "00:02:05:44 — ★ Favorite", "00:02:08:27 — ✗ Negative"; beside it a small grid of frame thumbnails (drawn rectangles). An arrow goes into a simple agent drawn as a terminal box with a blinking cursor.
scenes.caption: Plain text for your agent.
scenes.vo: Or save plain text, with frames — any AI agent reads it.

scenes.draw: Back to the player, one video. Keycap I on the beat: a [ bracket snaps onto the bar; keycap O: a ] snaps; the part between is hatched. Then on G(40) the player turns into a playlist: 4 files as rows, each row gets hatched [ ] segments, one per beat.

captions.text: Press I. Press O. Keep the good part.
One video — or the whole playlist.

scenes.vo: Now the real trick. Press I, press O — keep the good part. One video, or a whole playlist.

scenes.draw: On 38.04 the hatched segments lift off the rows and fly, in playlist order, onto ONE timeline track — end to end, markers riding along. Label "Premiere Pro". On G(56) a drawn hand grabs one cut point and nudges it slightly. Nothing else moves.

captions.text: One export. A ready rough cut.

scenes.vo: One export — Playlist Timeline XML — and the rough cut is already assembled. You just trim.

scenes.draw: Three small drawings appear one per beat-pair: a phone (vertical frame) for reels, a timeline for the editor, a terminal box for the agent with one line "Cut 00:00:12:10 → 00:00:18:02".
scenes.caption: Your reels. Your editor. Your agent.
scenes.vo: For your reels, your editor, or your agent.

scenes.draw: The real Mark Player icon (src-tauri/icons/128x128@2x.png) is wiped in by the marker, "Mark Player" written by hand under it, "FREE" stamped on a beat, then a small line "macOS · Windows · github.com/danilagoleen/mark-player". Fade to paper over the last 1.0 s.
scenes.caption: Video notes, pinned to the frame.
